evidence: Source inspection of Java CameraPath, ReplayViewer and ReplayPlayback, Rust CameraCurve/export_feed, camera.cjs and replay.cjs; no helper, classes, game or exports executed
sampleTime: Whole milliseconds plus remainder divided by denominator, matching the Rust evaluator's operation order
frameTime: Derives whole milliseconds and remainder from an exact bounded integer frame index, with FPS 1 through 120 for baked packet replays
bakedReplay: Camera poses use sampleForViewAt(frameTime(origin,index,fps)); packet timestamps retain the floored whole milliseconds. The final duration sample uses sampleForView as well.
nativeVideoFeed: The helper step uses the same sampleTime conversion for its existing rational timestamp. Rust export_feed expects sample_for_view_at followed by wire_pose, matching the helper's live sampleForView then wirePose path.
javaViewArguments: ReplayViewer.PATH casts CameraPath.at's double yaw, pitch and FOV to float when calling backend.camera; ReplayPlayback.camera receives float arguments and passes yaw to the player rotation fields
roundingOrder: Java-curve view sampling rounds the evaluated unwrapped yaw to float32 before equivalent-turn normalization for the Bedrock wire. Normalizing the double first can lose the Java float rounding step.
rawCurve: Raw sample/sample_at and saved keyframes are unchanged for editor evaluation. Explicit fixed cameras and non-Java interpolation keep their previous conversion rules.
bounds: Finite camera sampling from 0 through 86400000 milliseconds; no positive fraction at the maximum; integer denominator 1 through 1000; remainder within denominator; unsafe frame numerators rejected
